scripts.test:most: yarn security && yarn lint && yarn typecheck && rails test && yarn jest
scripts.test:all: yarn security && yarn lint && yarn typecheck && rails test && yarn jest && yarn test:cypress:run
scripts.test:all:mod: rails test && yarn jest && yarn test:cypress
scripts.//test:cypress:run: `-s command-Cypress`, not `-s last`. With `-k`, concurrently kills the server as soon as Cypress exits, so the *last* process to exit is always the server it just killed, reporting SIGTERM -- and `-s last` turned that into a failing exit code on a fully green suite. Both this and test:cypress:gate did it, so `yarn test:all` could not pass no matter what. Verified in isolation on 2026-09-22: Cypress passes -> 0, Cypress fails -> 1, server dies early (taking Cypress with it) -> 1. See UPGRADE_PLAN 8e item 13.
scripts.test:cypress:run: concurrently -p "[{name}]" -n "Server,Cypress" -k -s command-Cypress -c yellow,green "yarn testServer" "yarn cypress run --project ./spec"
scripts.test:cypress:gate: yarn testPacks && concurrently -p "[{name}]" -n "Server,Cypress" -k -s command-Cypress -c yellow,green "yarn testServer" "yarn cypress run --project ./spec"
scripts.//typecheck: Two programs, not one. tsconfig.json excludes test/, so `tsc --noEmit` alone never looks at a single Jest test -- which mattered on 2026-09-18, when typecheck was green while test/javascript/util/arrayUtils.test.ts did not compile at all. Jest reported that as "Test suite failed to run", which reads like a broken test rather than a type error, and the suite count silently fell from 125 to 108. A suite that fails to compile subtracts its tests from the total instead of failing them, so watch the count, not just the pass line. See UPGRADE_PLAN 8e item 11.
scripts.//testPacks: The `||` clause is not defensive padding, it closes a hole in the gate. Shakapacker records the compilation digest even when webpack FAILED, so the next run finds the digest current, prints "Everything's up-to-date", and exits 0 -- handing Cypress the last *good* bundle while the source does not compile. Reproduced deterministically on 2026-09-22: run 1 exit 1 with 15 error lines, run 2 exit 0, broken source untouched. Deleting the digest on failure forces the next run to rebuild and fail again, honestly. See UPGRADE_PLAN 8e item 12.

jest.//: ts-jest 29 takes its options from the transform entry, not from `globals`, and the option is `tsconfig` (the old `tsConfig` spelling is gone). The key matches the js-with-babel preset's own ts key exactly, so this overrides that entry rather than adding a second one -- jest merges a preset's transform map with the config's, and .js still goes through babel-jest.
